{{more citations needed|date=July 2011}}
'''Regularized canonical correlation analysis''' is a way of using [[ridge regression]] to solve the [[singularity theory|singularity]] problem in the [[cross-covariance matrix|cross-covariance matrices]] of [[canonical correlation analysis]]. By converting <math>\operatorname{cov}(X, X)</math> and <math>\operatorname{cov}(Y, Y)</math> into <math>\operatorname{cov}(X, X) + \lambda I_X</math> and <math>\operatorname{cov}(Y, Y) + \lambda I_Y</math>, it ensures that the above matrices will have reliable [[Matrix inverse|inverses]].

The idea probably dates back to [[Hrishikesh Vinod|Hrishikesh D. Vinod]]'s publication in 1976 where he called it "Canonical ridge".<ref>{{Cite Q | Q130748684 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite Q | Q28842820 }}</ref>
It has been suggested for use in the analysis of [[functional neuroimaging]] data as such data are often singular.<ref>{{Cite Q | Q129222383 }}</ref>
It is possible to compute the regularized canonical vectors in the lower-dimensional space.<ref>{{Cite thesis
 | author = Finn Årup Nielsen
 | year = 2001
 | title = Neuroinformatics in Functional Neuroimaging
 | url = http://www2.imm.dtu.dk/pubdb/views/edoc_download.php/201/pdf/imm201.pdf
 | publisher = [[Technical University of Denmark]]
}} Section 3.18.5</ref>
